title: Case: Customer complains about two click-and-collect grocery orders on consecutive days
context: Orders BP-2616 and BP-7112 were click-and-collect orders from Pebblewick Pantry's Saltmarsh Row store. No Plover Arc shipment exists for either; the customer wrote to the desk through the Customer portal.
initial_request: I wish to make a formal complaint regarding orders BP-2616 and BP-7112, both click and collect from your Saltmarsh Row store. 1. My husband, my seven-year-old and I all have influenza. My temperature this afternoon was 39.1. We chose click and collect on both days for one reason: so that nobody from this household would have to walk into a shop. 2. On 11 January order BP-2616 was short by one item. The store accepted the error and told me to come back for it. I did not. 3. Today, 12 January, I collected order BP-7112 at 16:10 and on unpacking found that one entire bag of four was missing: the chicken, the butter, the soup and my son's yoghurts, which is to say tonight's dinner. I telephoned. The store accepted the error and told me the bag is at the counter and I may collect it before 20:00. 4. That is the second time in two days that your mistake is to be put right by a sick person driving back and going inside. I am requesting that the missing bag be delivered to my address this evening at no charge, and that the cost of BP-7112 be refunded. I would be grateful for a reply from a person and not a template.

events.body: Order BP-2616 collected today from Saltmarsh Row. One item missing (oat milk, 2 cartons, charged). The store confirmed by telephone that it was left off and told me to return to collect it. I am unwell and will not be doing so. Please record this.
BP-2616, click and collect, Saltmarsh Row: customer reports one charged item missing and says she is unwell and cannot return to the store. Can the item be sent to her?

Not ours. Collection orders are picked and held by the store, we never see them. For what it's worth our home-delivery van passes Saltmarsh Row on the evening run, leaves here 18:30, and could carry a store transfer if the store duty manager raises one before 18:00. We can't raise it and we can't decide it; store orders and anything on charges or refunds for them belong to the store duty manager. They take requests by Email.

events.from: Collection counter staff, Pebblewick Pantry Saltmarsh Row
events.body: Copying the desk as the customer says she has written to you. BP-7112 collected 16:10. Bag 3 of 4 (chilled) was left in our chiller in error. Customer has phoned, we have apologised. The bag is in the chiller at the counter for her to collect up to close at 20:00.

acceptable_actions.recipient: Store duty manager, Pebblewick Pantry Saltmarsh Row
acceptable_actions.summary: Ask the store duty manager to decide whether the missing bag from BP-7112 can be got to the customer this evening without her returning, and to consider her refund request, saying the household has flu and this is the second error in two days.

must: Asks the store duty manager by Email to decide whether the missing bag from BP-7112 can be delivered to the customer this evening instead of her returning to the store

Tells the store duty manager that the household has influenza, that she used click and collect to avoid entering the store, and that this is the second short order in two days with the same 'come back for it' remedy
Passes on what Warehouse dispatch said as an option for the store to decide: the evening van leaves at 18:30 and could carry a store transfer if the store raises one before 18:00
Passes on her refund request for BP-7112 as a request for the store's decision
must_not: Tells the customer that the missing bag is ready for her to collect, or asks her to come back to the store
Promises her delivery this evening, free delivery, or a refund
Tells her the warehouse van will bring the bag before the store has raised or agreed a transfer
Gives advice about her illness, or about whether the chilled food is fine
Sends the request back to Warehouse dispatch, or tells her this is not a delivery matter and to contact the store herself
Treats the repeated copy of the request as a second, separate request (for example by sending two requests to the same team)
expected.reference_message: BP-7112 (and BP-2616), click and collect, customer Kestra Vexley. Your counter has told the desk that bag 3 of 4 from BP-7112 was left in the chiller and is held for her to collect by 20:00. She has written to say she cannot reasonably do that: she, her husband and her seven-year-old have influenza, and she chose click and collect on both days so nobody from the household would have to go into the store. This is the second short order in two days; on BP-2616 yesterday she was also told to come back. The missing bag is tonight's dinner. Request for your decision: can the bag be got to her address this evening instead? Warehouse dispatch say their home-delivery van leaves at 18:30, passes Saltmarsh Row and could carry a store transfer if you raise one before 18:00; they cannot raise or decide it themselves. She has also asked for delivery at no charge and for the cost of BP-7112 to be refunded; both are yours to decide and I have promised her neither. She has asked for a reply from a person. Please tell me what you decide so I can tell her accurately.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2608: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. The escalation message arrives twice; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
